source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
The exact amount of water corn needs must be adjusted according to its growth stage. Early in growth, corn needs relatively little water -- roughly 30 to 50% of its total need -- because the plant is still building its root system before tasseling/flowering. As the plant approaches flowering, water need increases sharply to about 50 to 70% of total need.

If, during the stage when corn is still small, there happens to be a heavy or prolonged rain event, water can accumulate and pool around the base of the plant; farmers should promptly drain excess water away from the field so it does not sit and cause root damage or disease.
